svg.title: Two surfactants lower surface tension yet scarcely change droplet counts at a simulated smoke-cloud edge
svg.desc: Head-and-tail symbols grouped along a short arc of the droplet surface also mark the two cloud-model cases containing surfactant. Dodecyl sulfate lowered surface tension more than octyl sulfate at one tenth the molar dose. Moving where dry, smoky air entered the cloud increased the total at 100 m above cloud base by 89.0 droplets/cm³ with matched acid seeds or finite surfactant supply, and by 66.7/cm³ with surface tension fixed at the laboratory values.
